history.period: Built 1936 (Maharaja Bhupinder Singh); Wikipedia infobox says 'Completed 1938' - conflict flagged
history.summary: Shri Kali Devi Temple is a Hindu temple on Mall Road, Patiala, opposite the Baradari Gardens, built in 1936 by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala (reigned 1900-1938). Inspired by the Kali temples of Bengal, the Maharaja brought a six-foot-tall black stone idol of Maa Kali and the Paawan Jyot (sacred flame) from Bengal/Calcutta to Patiala, and offered the first sacrifice of a water buffalo at the installation. The temple walls carry colourful murals of scenes from Hindu epics; several sources call it a national monument (claim, verify). An older shrine of Raj Rajeshwari stands in the middle of the complex. It is a kul devi of many families and draws large crowds during the Navratras, with devotees offering mustard oil, lentils, coconuts, bangles, and chunnis.

town_description: Patiala is a major city in southeastern Punjab and the historic capital of the former princely state of Patiala, founded in 1763 by Ala Singh. Known as the 'royal city', it holds palaces, forts, and important religious shrines.

travel.airport: Chandigarh Airport (~65 km - verify) is the nearest commercial airport.
travel.railway: Patiala railway station, in the city.
travel.road: On Mall Road, opposite the Baradari Gardens (next to Rajendra Tank); easy reach by city auto-rickshaw and taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratras (Sep-Oct and Mar-Apr) are the busiest - avoid the rush if seeking a quiet visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Timings not published in the consulted sources (verify); visitors suggest Tuesdays and Saturdays are busy but spiritually uplifting.
